In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and characterization of SLN formulations for anticancer drugs and the study of their in vitro cytotoxicity and cytotoxicity of their combination with other drugs.
the development of SLN for anticancer drug delivery, with the aim to improve the therapeutic efficacy and to reduce the side effects of anticancer therapy.
the development of SLN as drug carriers for the delivery of antineoplastic agents, and the evaluation of the antiprolifearative activity of these formulations on HT-29 colon cancer cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SLN are able to deliver drugs into the cancer cell with a better efficacy than conventional drug formulations, and this effect is enhanced by the combination of drugs.
SLN could represent an alternative drug delivery system for the treatment of solid tumors.
the SLN formulations are more effective than the conventional drug formulations, especially for the combination of low doses of cholesteryl butyrates and anticancer drugs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of cholesteryl butanoate SLN and conventional chemotherapy could represent a promising strategy for the treatment of colorectal carcinoma.

solid lipid nanoparticles could be a good alternative to conventional drug formulations for the treatment of colorectal cancer, and that the combination of low chol-but concentrations (0.1 mM and 0.2 mM, respectively) with low doxorubicin concentrations (1.72 and 1.17 n M, respectively) could be proposed as an effective antitumoral treatment.

the cytotoxic effect of anticancer drugs encapsulated in SLN is higher than that of the free drug, and the combination of cholesteryl butanoate and doxorubicil or paclitacel could exert a greater-than-additve antiproliferate effect on colorectal cancer cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of low doses of SLN carrying cholesteryl esters and conventional anticancer drugs could be a promising strategy to enhance anticancer drug efficacy and reduce drug-related toxicity.
SLN formulations can be used to deliver anticancer drugs and to enhance their antitumor activity, especially when combined with conventional drug formulations.
SLN can be proposed as an alternative drug delivery system, and that their cytotoxicity is enhanced in combination with other anticancer drugs, especially when they are incorporated in SLN.
